147.97571,-33.87844.name: DIR 164 — Canola (Brassica napus L.) field trial (site 8), Weddin Shire Council
147.97571,-33.87844.type: Canola (Brassica napus L.), licensed field trial
147.97571,-33.87844.desc: WHAT. A licensed GMO crop field trial site, Herbicide tolerance, held by Monsanto Australia Limited. WHERE IT SITS. OGTR named the council area this site is in and published no coordinate on the page this was read from, so this marker sits in that council area and not at the trial itself. WHY IT MATTERS. OGTR names the council area of every licensed site, its area in hectares and the licence it runs under. No other register on this map states where a release is at all, which is the comparison worth making even at this resolution.

-86.81090,36.15230.name: The Center for Reproductive Health
-86.81090,36.15230.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Jaime M. Vasquez, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-93.26547,44.97730.name: Minneapolis Veterans Affairs Health Care System
-93.26547,44.97730.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Department of Veterans Affairs. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-60.63999,-32.94012.name: Servicio de Medicina Reproductiva- Instituto Gamma
-60.63999,-32.94012.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

-77.30640,38.84620.name: Fairfax Cryobank / California Cryobank — donor limits
-77.30640,38.84620.desc: Two of the largest US sperm banks. Family limits in the United States are voluntary, set by professional guidance rather than law, and counted by the bank from reported pregnancies — a figure that depends on recipients choosing to report. Cases of donors with dozens of confirmed offspring have emerged through consumer DNA matching rather than through any register, which is the pattern throughout this part of the industry: the technology that broke anonymity is also the only thing auditing it.

4.35200,50.84200.name: Corporate Europe Observatory
4.35200,50.84200.desc: Documents lobbying in the EU institutions, including on the new genomic techniques file. The Transparency Register publishes numbers; someone has to read them against meeting records to make them mean anything, and a small number of organisations do that work.

4.38000,50.84100.name: Data protection authorities — rights over your own genetic data
4.38000,50.84100.desc: Under the GDPR and comparable laws elsewhere, genetic data is a special category: you can demand a copy of what an organisation holds about you, require it to be corrected, and in most circumstances require it to be deleted — and complain to a regulator that can fine, without going to court. This is the strongest right an ordinary person has anywhere on this map, and it applies to consumer testing companies, biobanks and clinics alike. It became concrete when a company holding fifteen million genomes filed for bankruptcy and its database was listed as a saleable asset.

-1.05000,53.95000.name: Fera Science
-1.05000,53.95000.state: Sand Hutton, York — a joint venture with the UK government
-1.05000,53.95000.desc: The former UK Food and Environment Research Agency, now a joint venture in which the government retains a stake alongside a private partner, selling laboratory and field services and regulatory consultancy. Its own pitch is the notable part: it offers established working relationships with competent authorities as a reason to hire it. A body that was the state's own science agency, now selling access to the regulator's confidence as a commercial service, is a different object from either a government laboratory or an independent contractor, and this map has almost no other examples of the type.

4.90410,52.36760.name: EAZA Biobank
4.90410,52.36760.state: Amsterdam — European Association of Zoos and Aquaria
4.90410,52.36760.desc: The biobanking service for the European and Middle Eastern zoo and aquarium association, operating through national hubs rather than one central store — the United Kingdom hub sits in a purpose-built facility at Edinburgh Zoo with capacity for a further eighty thousand specimens. It is the institutional counterpart to the seed vaults on the crop side of this map: a network of captive-animal collections systematically preserving tissue, blood, serum, DNA and cell lines from the animals in their care. Whether that material is a conservation resource or a supply of starting material for the de-extinction ventures elsewhere in this facet is not decided by the biobank — it is decided by whoever is granted a loan from it.
